Motivation


In recent times, owning your data has become more and more relevant.
Many people use web-based spreadsheets as an important part of their lives.
Python is one of the most popular programming languages, but using it in spreadsheets hasn’t been really viable yet.
Creating very bespoke or ‘hyperpersonalized’1 software (either for self consumption or teams)

Before you try the repo code

🐳 docker and its docker compose plugin are required to run the demo material
🐍 Python tools/CLI/etc. should run with uv run or, more permanently, uv tool install <name>.
🛶 You don’t need tilt if you don’t want the fancy webpage with hot reload, just use docker compose up and look at the ports.
🤖 For the AI examples, I’ve used OpenRouter, but you can use any AI provider you’d like.

title: Teaching Some Python to Your Spreadsheets
text:
What is grist?


Grist is a modern relational spreadsheet. It combines the flexibility of a spreadsheet with the robustness of a database.
It can run:

locally (docker or desktop)
in the cloud or homelab
like Google Docs at https://getgrist.com





It stores everything as a SQLite database that is easy to share and backup

section: A CLI client for the API
text:
A CLI client for the API
pygrister is a Python library and a CLI for grist 1
It requires a URL and an API key, but additional configuration can be passed.
In this example, .env2 is the file we could use in our workshop repo:
GRIST_API_KEY=<your user api key>
GRIST_SELF_MANAGED=Y
GRIST_SELF_MANAGED_HOME=http://localhost:8484
GRIST_SELF_MANAGED_SINGLE_ORG=N
GRIST_SERVER_PROTOCOL=http
GRIST_TEAM_SITE=docs
If you cloned the repo, it will be available with uv run (or uvx --from pygrister gry).This file needs to be created as the demo data lives in docker volumes

title: Teaching Some Python to Your Spreadsheets
text:
Model Context Protocol


mcp-server-grist is an MCP server written in Python. It allows AI applications like Claude, IBM Bob, Codex, pi, OpenClaw, Hermes, etc. to connect to the Grist API.



This is not the official MCP that lives in https://<yoursite>.getgrist.com/mcp for the commercial version, so authentication will use the same API keys instead of OAuth2.





To run mcp-server-grist with uv we need these two environment variables:

GRIST_API_KEY (user or Service Account)
GRIST_API_URL (this will be where Grist is running + /api)

title: Teaching Some Python to Your Spreadsheets
text:
Safer use of AI

Hermes will learn over time, this is a helpful feature.
LLMs can be too smart and try to achieve a goal in unintended ways, so using a Grist service account key instead of a user key can reduce the things it can break.
Additionally, we can make different types of copies (templates, structure-only copies) to prevent Hermes from breaking things.
